workflows.name: Typhoon & Calamity Demand-Surge Forecasting and Pre-Positioning

Automation Opportunity: - PAGASA-feed → surge-scenario auto-run (forecast SKU spike, gap, pre-position plan) on Signal declaration, replacing manual Step 2
- Auto-flag of flood-control cluster SKUs whose on-hand + in-transit < modeled surge demand by region
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: per-region surge model calibrated on prior storms and refreshed pre-season; operational: post-event rebalancing to prevent stranded stock; operational: RA 7581 price-freeze interface (W5496)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pre-position-too-late risk**: import flood-control SKUs (45–90-day lead) arrive after the storm window; mitigated by pre-season build and local-source qualification per region
- **Over-preposition/stranded-stock risk**: storm veers off, leaving region overstocked; mitigated by post-event inter-island rebalancing (W5492) and the seasonal sell-down into steady-state demand
- **Price-gouging/compliance risk**: surge demand collides with the RA 7581 calamity price freeze; mitigated by the W5496 interface so pre-positioning never sets up an un-frozen price
System Touchpoints: - S&OP/what-if platform (links to W3917); demand-sensing signals incl. PAGASA feed (links to W3910); supply/import (links to VS-02/VS-122); DC/WMS (links to VS-04); fleet/3PL (links to VS-06/VS-110); inter-island transfer (links to W5492); DTI price-freeze (links to W5496); BCP/disaster response (links to VS-69)
Time Estimate: - Pre-season model refresh ~3–5 days/yr; per-storm scenario + pre-positioning ~8–16 hrs; post-storm sell-down/rebalancing absorbed in the weekly cycle

steps.activity: Demand Planning maintain a flood-control/calamity SKU cluster (sandbags, plywood, lumber, nails/screws, tarps, water pumps, flashlights/batteries, PVC pipes, waterproofing, generators) and a per-region surge model calibrated on prior storms (Haiyan/Yolanda, Odette/Rai, Karding) — base demand × Signal-strength × region exposure — refreshed each pre-season

On PAGASA forecast track, S&OP/IBP run the surge scenario for the likely landfall region: forecast SKU spike, days-of-supply gap vs on-hand + in-transit, and the pre-positioning plan (push build-forward from the nearest DC, expedite local sourcing links to VS-122/VS-03, inter-island transfer links to W5492) timed against the 45–90-day import lead where import SKUs are involved

S&OP/IBP/Supply execute pre-positioning (DC special-build, store forward-stocking of the calamity cluster, 3PL capacity pre-book links to VS-06/VS-110), set allocation/rationing rules for the event, interface the DTI price-freeze constraint (links to W5496), and run the post-storm sell-down/rebalancing to avoid stranded post-event stock

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Merchandising (links to VS-01/VS-101), Supply Planning, Sourcing/Import (links to VS-122), Marketing (links to VS-14/VS-58), DC Operations (links to VS-04), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-101)

fields.Volume: The largest demand quarter: holiday décor/gift items, lighting, appliances, furniture + renovation surge ahead of the holidays + 13th-month-pay-driven discretionary spend across 200 stores

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-generation of the ber-months phased import order plan from the demand profile and 45–90-day lead phasing
- Weekly sell-through-vs-plan auto-flag by category/region for in-season re-forecast triggers
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: prior-year-actuals demand profile with component segmentation; operational: weekly in-season sell-through re-forecast and burn-down; operational: RCCP capacity reservation for peak weeks
Pain Points / Risks: - **Import-lead-timing risk**: ber-months import SKUs ordered too late miss the Sep ramp; mitigated by the phased Jun–Jul order plan against the 45–90-day lead
- **Over-buy/obsolete risk**: optimistic holiday forecast leaves gift/décor carry-over; mitigated by weekly sell-through re-forecast and the post-holiday burn-down
- **Capacity-bind risk**: peak weeks exceed DC/store/3PL capacity; mitigated by RCCP reservation (links to W3918)
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; MFP/OTB (links to VS-101/W3922); import/sourcing (links to VS-122); DC (links to VS-04); store labor/WFM (links to VS-19.3); promo/marketing (links to VS-14/VS-58); seasonal clearance (links to VS-64); phase-out (links to W3908)
Time Estimate: - Annual plan ~1 week; weekly re-forecast Sep–Jan absorbed in the monthly cycle

steps.activity: Demand Planning build the ber-months demand profile per category/region from prior-year actuals (Sep ramp → Oct/Nov peak → Dec Noche Buena/Christmas peak → Jan drop), segment holiday-gift vs renovation-surge vs 13th-month-discretionary components, and size the peak vs steady-state lift

S&OP/IBP translate the profile into a phased supply/import pre-build that respects the 45–90-day import lead (order by Jun–Jul for Sep landfall), align to the MFP/OTB and markdown budget (links to VS-101/W3922), and reserve DC throughput, store-labor peak (links to VS-19.3), and 3PL capacity (links to VS-06/VS-110) for the peak weeks

S&OP/IBP run the in-season re-forecast (sell-through vs plan by week), trigger markdown/rebalance on under/over-performance (links to VS-101/VS-64), and plan the post-holiday clearance and inventory burn-down to hit turn and avoid obsolete carry-over (links to W3908 phase-out)

workflows.name: Summer Season (Aircon, Garden & Dry-Season Construction) Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-phasing of the import pre-build from the summer profile and 45–90-day lead
- Heat-wave/temperature-signal → short-cycle re-forecast auto-trigger (links to W3910)
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)
- operational: region-segmented summer profile incl. construction uplift; operational: demand-sensing-driven in-season re-forecast; operational: install-capacity reservation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Heat-wave-timing risk**: aircon demand spikes with the first heat wave, which is hard to date precisely; mitigated by demand sensing (W3910) and forward-stocking ahead of the window
- **Install-bottleneck risk**: aircon sell-through outruns install/service capacity; mitigated by reserving install capacity in Step 2 (links to VS-12)
- **Import-timing risk**: aircon import SKUs ordered too late miss the Mar peak; mitigated by the Dec–Jan order phasing
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; MFP/OTB (links to VS-101); import/sourcing (links to VS-122); install/services (links to VS-12); DC (links to VS-04); demand sensing (links to W3910); B2B/trade (links to VS-11/VS-107/W5493)
Time Estimate: - Annual plan ~1 week; weekly re-forecast Mar–Jun absorbed in the monthly cycle

steps.activity: Demand Planning build the summer demand profile: aircon/appliance heat-wave elasticity, garden/outdoor seasonality, water-tank/pump demand, and the dry-season construction uplift on lumber/cement/steel/tools (trade/B2B links to VS-11/VS-107/W5493), segmented by region (summer hits different regions on different timing)

S&OP/IBP phase the supply/import pre-build (aircon/appliances are import-heavy, 45–90-day lead → order by Dec–Jan), align to OTB (links to VS-101), and reserve install/service capacity (links to VS-12) and DC/3PL capacity for the aircon bulky-flow and the construction-material volume

S&OP/IBP run in-season re-forecast driven by actual heat/temperature and construction-permit activity signals (demand sensing links to W3910), trigger rebalance/expedite on heat-wave spikes, and manage the aircon installation backlog and the post-summer garden sell-down

workflows.name: Inter-Island Inventory Rebalancing and Allocation Under Disruption

Automation Opportunity: - Disruption-signal → imbalance-quantification auto-run (gap vs demand by region/DC) replacing manual Step 1
- Allocation-rule engine auto-suggesting rationed allocation by priority on declaration
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: explicit allocation priority rules (A-item/contractual/margin); operational: post-event reconciliation and structural-pattern feed to network design; operational: multi-carrier inter-island redundancy
Pain Points / Risks: - **Island-transport-availability risk**: inter-island RORO/batch capacity is itself disrupted by the same storm; mitigated by multi-carrier relationships and pre-positioning (W5489)
- **Allocation-fairness/contract risk**: rationing starves B2B/contractual customers; mitigated by explicit priority rules (A-item, contractual, margin) in Step 2
- **Band-aid-vs-structural risk**: repeated rebalancing masks a structural network gap; mitigated by feeding patterns into VS-136/W3923
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; DC/WMS (links to VS-04); inter-island freight (links to VS-06/VS-66/VS-110); allocation/rationing; substitute master (links to W279); network design/MEIO (links to VS-136/W3923); import constraints (links to W3915)
Time Estimate: - Per-event response ~8–16 hrs; monthly structural rebalance ~1–2 days

steps.activity: S&OP/IBP/Supply detect the regional imbalance or disruption impact: affected DC/region, days-of-supply by SKU, port/RORO/batch availability (links to VS-06/VS-66), and quantify the gap vs demand, including the typhoon-surge case (links to W5489) and the import-port-congestion case (links to W3915)

S&OP/IBP decide the reallocation: inter-island transfer from surplus DCs (links to VS-04/VS-06/VS-66), rationed allocation to stores prioritized by A-item/service/contractual obligation (B2B links to W5493), substitute SKU mapping (links to W279/VS-01), and expedite/alternate-port sourcing where the disruption is prolonged

S&OP/IBP execute and track the rebalancing (transfer orders, RORO/inter-island dispatch, allocation holds), reconcile post-event, and feed the structural-imbalance pattern into network design (links to VS-136/W3923) and the next cycle's safety-stock policy

fields.Participants: Trade/B2B Sales (links to VS-11/VS-107), Demand Planning, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Supply Planning, Sourcing/Import (links to VS-122/VS-182), Finance (links to VS-105/VS-181), Store Ops/DC (links to VS-07/VS-04), Project/Indent (links to VS-182)

workflows.name: B2B / Trade-Project Demand Induction into the Consensus Plan

Automation Opportunity: - Pipeline → project-demand-overlay auto-build from the trade CRM/quote system
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: project-demand kept as a separate overlay on the baseline; operational: probability-weighted reservation with separate forecast-accuracy tracking; operational: import-lead reconciliation against required-by dates
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lumpy-distortion risk**: project demand folded into the statistical baseline bullwhips steady-state replenishment; mitigated by the separate project-demand overlay
- **Win-probability-optimism risk**: pipeline never converts, leaving reserved stock; mitigated by probability-weighted reservation and separate accuracy tracking
- **Lead-time-miss risk**: large project BOM with import components misses the required-by date; mitigated by the 45–90-day lead reconciliation in Step 2
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; trade/key-account (links to VS-11/VS-107); indent/bulk (links to VS-182); import/sourcing (links to VS-122); jobsite/material staging (links to VS-77/VS-74/VS-04); project finance (links to VS-181/VS-105); forecast accuracy (links to W3911)
Time Estimate: - Monthly ~2–3 days; per major win ~0.5–1 day

steps.activity: Trade/B2B Sales provide the qualified project pipeline (project, SKU/BOM, volume, required-by date, win-probability, indent/special-order flags links to VS-182/VS-107); Demand Planning translate it into a project-demand overlay on the statistical baseline, kept separate from steady-state so lumpy demand does not distort replenishment

S&OP/IBP/Supply reconcile project demand against supply constraints (import lead 45–90 days links to VS-122, vendor capacity, DC staging links to VS-77/VS-04, jobsite delivery links to VS-74), decide make-to-stock vs make/order-to-order vs indent, and reserve capacity/material for high-probability projects

S&OP/IBP fold confirmed project demand into the constrained consensus plan (links to W3912/W3920), align financing (project escrow/lien links to VS-181, SCF links to VS-105), and track project-demand forecast accuracy separately (links to W3911) so project phasing errors are visible

workflows.name: New-Store-Opening Demand Induction and Initial-Stock S&OP

Automation Opportunity: - Comparable-store → new-store induction-curve auto-build by size/region
- 13-week ramp actual-vs-curve auto-flag for rebalance triggers
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: induction aligned to the consensus plan to avoid starving existing stores; operational: 13-week ramp tracking with rebalance; operational: ramp-learning fed back into comparable-store models
Pain Points / Risks: - **Starve-existing-stores risk**: initial-stock drop pulls inventory from the shared DC pool; mitigated by consensus-plan alignment in Step 2
- **Over-stock-new-store risk**: optimistic induction over-stocks a new store; mitigated by the ramp curve and 13-week rebalance
- **Import-timing risk**: opening-date slip vs import landfall; mitigated by lead-time-buffer in the import pre-build
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; assortment/allocation (links to VS-01/VS-55); store opening (links to VS-37/VS-20); DC (links to VS-04); logistics (links to VS-06/VS-110); import (links to VS-122); analytics (links to VS-28.1); forecast accuracy (links to W3911)
Time Estimate: - Per opening ~3–5 days induction; 13-week ramp tracking absorbed in the weekly cycle

steps.activity: Demand Planning build the new-store demand induction: initial assortment/stocking by store size/region (links to VS-01/VS-55), the grand-opening-week spike model from comparable-store history, and the 13-week ramp-to-steady-state curve, segmented by new-vs-mature-store-region

S&OP/IBP/Supply schedule the initial-stock build and inbound (DC pick/pack + inbound to the new store links to VS-04/VS-06) against the opening date, pre-build import SKUs against the 45–90-day lead (links to VS-122), and align the opening to the consensus plan so the induction does not starve existing stores

S&OP/IBP track the ramp actual vs the induction curve weekly for the first 13 weeks, trigger rebalance/replenishment tuning on over/under-performance, and feed ramp-learning back into comparable-store models (links to W3911) and network demand for the next openings

workflows.name: Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) and Consignment S&OP Integration

Automation Opportunity: - Consensus-demand + POS/sell-through auto-share to VMI vendors against agreed min/max
- VMI/consignment service-level auto-scorecard feed to the vendor scorecard
Controls: - CTL-613 (ensure controlled execution — Calamity, Seasonality & Philippine-Retail Demand–Supply Dynamics (PA-127.4).)

- operational: VMI/consignment as a distinct treatment to prevent double-planning; operational: consignment ownership-transfer settlement (VS-170/VS-05); operational: VMI service-level feed to vendor scorecard
Pain Points / Risks: - **Double-planning risk**: VMI/consignment SKUs planned both by BuildRight supply and the vendor, over-ordering; mitigated by the distinct treatment in Step 1
- **Ownership-boundary/ settlement risk**: consignment ownership-transfer mis-settled at POS; mitigated by the VS-170/VS-05 settlement control
- **Vendor-signal-lag risk**: VMI vendor does not react to BuildRight demand; mitigated by shared signal and the vendor scorecard
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; VMI/consignment (links to VS-45); inventory/ownership (links to VS-05/VS-170); POS/sell-through (links to VS-08); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67/VS-03); SCF (links to VS-105); inventory policy (links to VS-136/W3914)
Time Estimate: - Monthly ~1–2 days; continuous monitoring absorbed in the cycle

steps.activity: S&OP/IBP reconcile VMI/consignment demand into the consensus plan as a distinct treatment: VMI SKUs where the vendor owns the replenishment signal (links to VS-45), consignment where BuildRight sells-but-does-not-own until point-of-sale (links to VS-05/VS-170), so they are visible but not double-planned against BuildRight-owned supply

S&OP/IBP/Vendor-Management coordinate the vendor signal: share the consensus demand and POS/sell-through data with VMI vendors, agree min/max and service levels, manage the consignment settlement/ownership-transfer at POS, and align to SCF/consignment financing (links to VS-105/VS-170)

S&OP/IBP monitor VMI/consignment service level (stockout, overstock, vendor fill-rate), resolve signal/ownership-boundary disputes, and feed VMI performance into the vendor scorecard (links to VS-67/VS-03) and the inventory-policy review (links to VS-136/W3914)

workflows.name: Government-Mandated Price Events and Calamity Price-Freeze S&OP Response

Automation Opportunity: - Mandate-declaration → frozen-SKU scope + margin/demand-impact auto-assessment replacing manual Step 1
- Auto-suspension of conflicting promos on freeze-declaration
Controls: - operational: RA 7581 price-freeze scope/skus/regions/duration confirmed by Legal before execution; operational: price-freeze master + DTI price-check compliance (VS-118/W107); operational: promo-conflict auto-suspension
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-compression risk**: a freeze on calamity SKUs compresses margin exactly when demand spikes; mitigated by quantifying the gap for exec S&OP and SCF/financing (links to VS-105)
- **Non-compliance/penalty risk**: selling frozen SKUs above the ceiling or failing the DTI price-check; mitigated by the price-freeze master control and compliance monitoring (VS-118/W107)
- **Promo-conflict risk**: an active promo conflicts with the freeze; mitigated by Step 2 promo suspension/re-price
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; price master/freeze (links to VS-01.2/VS-118/W468/W107); promo/coupon (links to VS-14/VS-58); MFP/margin (links to VS-101); typhoon pre-positioning (links to W5489); regulatory (links to VS-22/VS-76/VS-117); exec S&OP (links to W3919)
Time Estimate: - Per mandate ~8–16 hrs assessment + execution; post-freeze reconciliation ~1–2 days

steps.activity: On a price-freeze/SRP mandate, Legal/Regulatory confirm scope (SKUs, regions, duration, price ceiling per RA 7581/DTI — links to VS-117/VS-22), and S&OP/IBP/Merchandising-Pricing assess the margin and demand impact: frozen SKUs' margin compression, the demand spike a freeze/calamity typically triggers, and the conflict with any active promo (links to VS-14/VS-58)

S&OP/IBP adjust the consensus plan: pull forward / re-phase demand for frozen SKUs, suspend/re-price conflicting promos, align the typhoon pre-positioning (links to W5489) so pre-positioned calamity stock is sold at the frozen price, and quantify the margin/demand gap for exec S&OP (links to W3912/W3919)

S&OP/IBP/Store Ops execute the frozen-price replenishment (no margin-driven stockout, no price-gouging — the freeze forbids it), monitor compliance (price-check links to VS-118/W107), and run the post-freeze demand/margin reconciliation and promo re-activation
